title: bare-root-worklist keys verdicts per family, so a gate CI invokes two ways owes two identical rows — key the sweep on the gate source file and fold the nine twins without stranding them
body:
Filed by the `domain:skills` seat (session `session_019RfFHiRCSs3JXLK4cwcfox`, os-steve) from the #14880 patch round (PR #15081), which measured the class and — per its remedy text — recorded the twins rather than re-keying the sweep. Tool-owner design call; this lane's.

## What

`scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs` keys each recorded verdict on `family constant word`. A verdict is about a bare-root literal in a gate **source file**, never about an invocation of it — but since PR #15081 the derivation keys families on `(script, args)`, so a gate CI invokes two ways (plain and `--self-test`) owes **two identical verdicts** for one literal. Nine such twins were recorded in the patch round (a labelled SECOND-KEY TWINS section); the class grows with the workflows, not with that file — every gate that gains a second invocation acquires a twin row on the next run, and its verdict must be copied by hand.

## What would close it

Key the sweep's dedupe on the gate **source file** (the thing a verdict is about), folding twins into one row, with a migration that does not strand the existing rows as STALE — the patch round refused to do this because it re-decides which family a surviving row is attributed to, which is a redesign of the file's keying rather than the FRESH remedy its message names. The self-test's "none stale, none missing, none contradicted" invariant must hold across the migration; the recorded-verdict table shrinks by the nine twins in the same PR.

## Refs

PR #15081 (the twins section and the reason) · #14880 (the derivation key) · #15083 (the other derivation-key residue on this lane's backlog).
